To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Raman spectroscopy can be used for direct analysis of biological macromo- lecules in single living cells and in chromosomes; (ii) confocal Raman microscopy provides the spatial resolution needed to study single cells or chromosomes; (iii) the method can be used for quantitative analysis of the composition and conformation of DNA and proteins in the cell nucleus and chromosomes.

(1) Raman microspectrometry is a highly sensitive, noninvasive, non-destructive, and label-free method to study the structure and conformation of biological macromolec-ules in living single cells, (2) the method can be used to characterize the composition and conformation of DNA–protein chromosomal substructures, (3) the method can detect changes of DNA conformation in response to environmental changes and (4) the method can distinguish between normal and abnormal cells

the Raman spectra of single living cells and single chromosomes are different from those of the same cells or chromosomes after fixation, that the Raman spectrum of a single living cell can be obtained in a few seconds and that Raman microspectrometry can be used to study living cells and chromosomes in situ, without the need for any special treatment.

the application of confocal Raman microscopy to the analysis of biological macromolecular systems.
the development and application of Raman spectroscopy to the study of single cells and chromosomes.
